subject: Request: API-key spend + latency jitter telemetry lens for Console
messages:
From: nikhil.sharma@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Cc: alice@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: API-key spend + latency jitter telemetry lens for Console

Team —

Quick ask from product: Acme Health raised a support ticket (HS-4532) today asking for a single Console view that helps them debug two correlated problems quickly: per-API-key spend spikes and sudden increases in tail/jitter for the same API keys. Right now they flip between the token-cost explorer and the trace UI and lose time mapping requests to API keys.

What I'm proposing (high level):
- A new “API-key lens” tile in Console that surfaces: 1) cost/time series per API key (token cost per hour), 2) 50/90/99 latency percentiles and jitter (P90 - P10), 3) quick links to a sample trace set and the top 5 request prompts by token usage.
- Ability to pivot by model family and quantization profile (so they can see whether a q4 variant reduced cost but increased jitter)
- Sampling controls: configurable window (1h/6h/24h) and an option to expand sampled traces for a selected spike.

Constraints/notes:
- We should avoid retaining full request payloads in the tile; link out to traces stored in the existing trace retention policy.
- This needs to be reasonably low-cost for customers; suggest we default to aggregated histograms and sampled traces.

Can product + console engineering align on feasibility and a rough timeline? Acme would like a prototype they can try by the end of the quarter, but I appreciate that’s aggressive.

Thanks —
Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
PM, Console & Observability
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: api-key-lens-mockup.png (image/png)]

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: nikhil.sharma@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: API-key spend + latency jitter telemetry lens for Console

Nikhil —

This is a good customer-driven ask. A couple of clarifying questions from my side before I scope: 
1) When you say “cost per hour per API key,” do you want raw token spend or normalized spend (i.e., cost normalized for model/variant so customers can compare across models)? Normalized helps with cross-model comparison but requires us to surface the pricing profile applied.
2) For the jitter metric: do you want a simple P90-P10 delta, or a more robust metric like interquartile range plus a spike detector? We can start with P90/P99 and a simple delta if speed to prototype matters.
3) Sampling: what is the acceptable sample rate for Acme? If they want to expand to 100% traces for a selected hour that will be expensive on our side unless we pull from existing retained traces.

I'll put together a short mockup and rough data model this afternoon and flag any blocking telemetry gaps. If Soojin can advise on the data retention/sampling costs, we can have a quick sync tomorrow.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sampling-cost-estimates.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: soojin.lee@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, nikhil.sharma@redwood.com
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: API-key spend + latency jitter telemetry lens for Console

Thanks — quick infra readout: 

1) Data availability: We have token-level ingest keyed by API key already, and we record per-request latency histograms at the gateway. Correlating them is straightforward if the ingestion includes the api_key_id; current p99 calculations are available as pre-aggregates in the metrics pipeline.

2) Cost: estimating two shapes — aggregated histograms (cheap) vs. expanded traces (expensive):
   - Aggregated lens (hourly histograms + percentiles): marginal storage increase ~2-3% for metrics DB, query cost negligible with pre-aggregates.
   - On-demand expanded traces for a selected hour: we can surface 50 sampled traces pulled from existing trace storage; pulling 100% is not acceptable without a customer commitment (spike could be thousands of traces).

3) Implementation approach:
   - Phase 1 (prototype, 2–3 sprints): UI + aggregated histograms, model/variant pivot, basic drill-out links to trace timestamps. No extra retention.
   - Phase 2 (canary): sampled trace expansion and an opt-in high-sample mode (enterprise-only toggle) that routes sampled data to a short-term store for deeper inspection.

Blocking questions for PM/Console UI:
- We need to decide whether normalized spend is computed client-side (UI applies pricing profile) or server-side (metrics pipeline materializes normalized cost). Server-side would be cleaner for performance but needs a small pipeline job.

Happy to take the lead on the infra plan if we agree on the scope.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior SRE, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: API-key spend + latency jitter telemetry lens for Console

Thanks all — short summary and proposed next steps: 

Summary decisions: 
- Start with aggregated histograms for the prototype (Phase 1). We'll show raw token spend and a normalized-cost overlay per model variant (server-side materialized, per Soojin's suggestion).
- Jitter metric = P90 and P99 plus a simple P90-P10 delta column. We can iterate to a richer spike detector in Phase 2.
- Traces: provide an expand-to-sample view (default 50 traces pulled from retention) — opt-in enterprise high-sample mode scoped to dedicated customers only.

Action items / owners: 
- Marissa: mockup + acceptance criteria for Phase 1 (due: Apr 11) — use the Figma link in related_links.
- Soojin: infra spec for server-side normalized-cost materialization + sampling plan (due: Apr 13).
- Grace: UX copy and how this shows up in the Console home tiles (due: Apr 13).
- Nikhil: coordinate with Acme and schedule a short demo of the prototype when available; I’ll also add HS-4532 to the priority board.

Timeline request: aiming for a prototype (Phase 1) by Apr 26 to demo to Acme next week. If we need to slide, call it out in your deliverable updates.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround on this.

Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
PM, Console & Observability
Redwood Inference
